contradictions.fact: Total gain/loss (gain_ft/loss_ft) vs itinerary day totals

claims.says: 3900/3900 for the camp(6,300 ft)-to-summit(8,459 ft) leg, a rise of only 2,159 ft per the route's own waypoints
about 5,700 ft of gain

contradictions.why: The header/stats gain_ft (5,659) matches the trailhead(2,800 ft)-to-summit(8,459 ft) elevation change shown by the route's own waypoints and the approach prose ('about 5,700 ft'), but the itinerary's day totals sum to 7,200 ft (27% higher), and day 2 alone claims 3,900 ft of gain/loss for a leg that the waypoints show as only 2,159 ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft/loss_ft (5,659) is corroborated by waypoint elevations and the approach text; itinerary day 2's 3,900 ft gain/loss figure looks like the error.

contradictions.fact: seasonal_guidance and partner_requirements describe the separate, glaciated Lyman-side approach instead of this non-glaciated Trinity-side route

claims.says: Class 3-4 + glacier
Late July through early September, while the Lyman Glacier still holds continuous snow/ice cover
Best combination of stable weather and continuous glacier snow cover before late-season melt-out
Long - typically a full day to reach a high camp near Spider Gap or Lyman Lakes before a summit push
Glacier travel and roped crevasse rescue ... Comfort leading/following 2-3 pitches of moderate snow/ice
Advanced - prior glacier travel and roped crevasse-rescue experience required
Strenuous multi-day approach (Phelps Creek to Spider Gap/Lyman Lakes high camp)
the standard southwest route described here is a non-glaciated, largely cross-country scramble
N/A - the standard southwest route is non-glaciated and does not cross the Lyman Glacier remnant, which lies on a separate, more involved approach on the mountain's northeast side
No rope, rack, or crevasse-rescue gear is needed on this side of the mountain unless you detour onto the glaciated NE (Lyman Glacier) side
this is a different basecamp than Lyman Lake/Spider Gap, which serves the separate, glaciated NE side of Chiwawa

contradictions.why: The Partners-tab requirements and part of the seasonal guidance describe a roped glacier climb approached via Phelps Creek/Spider Gap/Lyman Lakes, while overview, approach, waypoints, road, pro_needs, gear, detailed_rack, hazards and pro_tips all describe a non-glaciated Class 2-3 scramble from the Trinity Trailhead via Chiwawa River Road. A climber checking Partners would be told this needs glacier-travel/crevasse-rescue skills it doesn't.
contradictions.internal_resolution: 8+ fields agree on the Trinity/non-glaciated framing, including an explicit statement that this basecamp is different from the 'glaciated NE side' one; partner_requirements and the glacier language in seasonal_guidance/grade appear to be copied from that other, glaciated approach and are wrong here.

contradictions.fact: Direction of travel from camp to the Fortress-Chiwawa col

claims.says: The route follows the path of least resistance from Fortress-Chiwawa Col, traversing east-northeast aiming for the col
Chiwawa Basin high camp benches (lng -120.896283) sit EAST of the Fortress-Chiwawa col (lng -120.903268)
Fortress Mountain (8,760'), lies about 1.1 miles west across the Fortress-Chiwawa col

contradictions.why: beta says the party travels east-northeast to reach the col, but the route's own waypoint coordinates and overview both place the col west of camp (toward Fortress Mountain); travelling east-northeast from camp moves away from, not toward, the col.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoint coordinates and the overview's 'west' description agree with each other; beta's 'east-northeast' looks like the error.

contradictions.fact: Route grade (Class 2) vs. the summit block's own stated difficulty (Class 3-4/4+)

claims.says: Class 2

Class 2 walk-up on the SW slopes; no rope or technical protection used on this specific line (other Cloudy Peak approaches have 3rd/4th class sections, but the SW Slopes route itself is non-technical)
pushes the route to Class 3-4 — don't mistake the easy approach for the whole picture
Class 4+
True summit gained by a short, exposed Class 3-4 scramble on the north side of the block
exposed, unprotected Class 3-4 summit block with a steep drop-off — many parties stop below the true summit
the final rock spire/summit block requires unprotected Class 3-4 moves with real exposure

contradictions.why: The route's own top-level grade/grade_num (Class 2) and rope_note ('this specific line...is non-technical') contradict the overview, hazards, watch_out, climbing_route and waypoint text, which all describe this same route's summit block as Class 3-4 or Class 4+ and exposed.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Six independent fields (overview, hazards, watch_out, climbing_route, waypoint note, itinerary schedule) agree the crux is Class 3-4/4+; only grade/grade_num/rope_note undercount it as Class 2/non-technical.

contradictions.fact: Trailhead/approach named in itinerary+timing (Holden Village) vs. everywhere else (Phelps Creek)

claims.says: Most parties reach Cloudy Peak via Holden Village (Lady of the Lake ferry across Lake Chelan, then bus to the village) and hike the Railroad Creek / Hart-Lyman Lake trail up the valley
retrace the Railroad Creek trail back down through Lyman Lake and Hart Lake to Holden Village in time for the return ferry
Most parties reach Cloudy Peak via Holden Village...hike the Railroad Creek / Hart-Lyman Lake trail
The standard approach starts at the Phelps Creek Trailhead...which is the one matching the round-trip distance (~39.6 km) and the Leavenworth/US-2 road drive
Phelps Creek Trailhead
"Phelps Creek and Spider Gap (standard)", "primary": true
Phelps Creek Trailhead

contradictions.why: The day-by-day itinerary and Published Times both narrate a Holden Village/Railroad Creek ferry trip, but the route's waypoints, approach text (self-declared as matching this record's stats), primary approach_variant, and approach_logistics all describe a different trailhead and trip (drive to Phelps Creek Trailhead, hike over Spider Gap). A climber following the itinerary would book a Lake Chelan ferry instead of driving to Phelps Creek.
contradictions.internal_resolution: waypoints, approach (explicitly says it 'matches' the recorded stats), approach_variants (marked primary), approach_logistics and road all agree on Phelps Creek/Spider Gap; itinerary and timing.sectionBreakdown's narrative appears to be copied from the alternate Holden Village approach_variant.

contradictions.fact: Crevasse/glacier hazard on Safety tab vs. the approach's own Spider Gap glacier crossing

claims.says: N/A - no glacier travel; the route climbs open heather and talus directly from Cloudy Pass to the summit, not the nearby Spider Glacier/snowfield
ascends the glacier/snowfield about 0.5 mile to Spider Gap (7,100 ft) — this is the crux of the approach...can have open crevasses and firm, icy conditions early season
early season brings open crevasses and firm refrozen snow
Spider Gap is the crux of the approach — a permanent snow/glacier slope...can hold open crevasses and firm icy snow early season

contradictions.why: The Safety tab's seasonal_hazards.crevasses flatly says 'no glacier travel,' but the Plan tab's approach, a waypoint, and the primary approach_variant all describe crossing the Spider Glacier/permanent snowfield with documented early-season open-crevasse risk to get to this route.
contradictions.internal_resolution: seasonal_hazards.crevasses is technically scoped to the final summit push (which is correct), but as worded it reads as a blanket denial of any crevasse exposure on the trip, which three other fields contradict.

contradictions.fact: Optional rappel of the class 4 step vs. explicit no-rappel descent

claims.says: harness and 30m rope for the glacier crossing and optional rappel of the class 4 step
A light rack (a few slings, a 30m rope) is worth having for the short, exposed class 4 moves near the summit notches, where some parties prefer to belay or rappel rather than solo them
a few slings and a small cam or nut let you belay or rappel that rather than solo it
Multiple trip reports for this route explicitly describe downclimbing the ascent line...and none report rappelling; this is a downclimb/walk-off route, not a rappel descent
If you are looking for rappel anchors on this route you will not find any; nothing on it is rappelled

contradictions.why: gear, detailed_rack and rope_note each present rappelling the class 4 step as an option some parties use, while rappels="0" and the detailed descent_text/baseFinding state emphatically that no rappelling occurs and no anchors exist anywhere on the route.
contradictions.internal_resolution: rappels=0, descent_text (citing multiple trip reports) and baseFinding's explicit 'you will not find any [rappel anchors]' are the more specific sources; the 'optional rappel' language in gear/detailed_rack/rope_note looks like generic boilerplate not supported by this route's own research.

contradictions.fact: Route name/aspect/face (South, SE) vs. the actual described terrain (East face, Northeast Ridge)

claims.says: South Route
SE
Southeast Glacier/Face
route climbs the Southeast Glacier (east-facing) and finishes on the upper Northeast Ridge

this route is listed as the South Route with a south-east aspect, and everything published about it describes the EAST-facing glacier remnant and the upper NORTH-EAST ridge. Navigate by the glacier and the notch, not by the compass point in the name.

contradictions.why: The route's own name/aspect/face fields say South/Southeast, but the detailed route description consistently describes an east-facing glacier and a Northeast Ridge finish — a mismatch the row itself flags.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own baseFinding text explicitly acknowledges and resolves this: treat name/aspect/face as inaccurate labels and follow the glacier+ridge description instead.

a core early-to-mid-summer window (roughly June into August) as the sweet spot...Dark Peak is broadly reckoned reasonably climbable May through October

gaining roughly 1,900 ft over about 6-7 miles to reach Spider Meadow...8-9 miles and roughly 2,500 ft above the trailhead

contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, climbing_route and itinerary are detailed and consistent with each other; beta's claim that none could be found is simply wrong, likely stale text left over from before enrichment.

contradictions.fact: seasonal_guidance/partner_requirements tie this route to the 'Lyman basin,' which this approach never reaches

claims.says: Mid-summer through early fall (roughly late July through September), once approach snow in the Lyman basin has consolidated or cleared
backpack in via the Phelps Creek Trail/Spider Meadow or the Lyman Lake/Cloudy Pass side to a high camp
the left branch carries on toward Spider Gap and Larch Knob, and the Dumbell path is the RIGHT-hand one

contradictions.why: This route's own approach_variants describe Dumbell's path as the branch that does NOT go to Spider Gap/Lyman Basin, yet seasonal_guidance explains the climbing window by reference to snow 'in the Lyman basin,' and partner_requirements offers the Lyman Lake/Cloudy Pass side as an approach option for this peak.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own approach_variants keep Dumbell's line in Phelps Basin, never crossing to Lyman Basin; the July-September date range itself isn't wrong (it matches best_season), only the stated terrain reference is misapplied, likely copied from a neighboring Lyman-basin peak's record.
